newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds climb on, set to hold new level.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds climb on, set to hold new level.

text.p: Danish bond prices swept ahead again on Tuesday, with the 2006 benchmark topping 110 and dealers expecting the new levels to hold up to the close.
"There are not many sellers in the market and that helps prices up. The thin trade means things could quickly change, but we should hold the present levels," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.30 point from the opening at 110.20, yielding 6.49 percent in turnover of 2.8 billion crowns while its December future rose 0.26 point to 109.94 with 312 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.65 point to 87.30.
The crown traded at 3.8261 per mark at 1135 gmt, up from around 3.8270 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 91 basis points after being as narrow as 88 during the morning. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969652
